item.title: PIO diplomat criticises UK foreign office for being woke, quits
item.description: A senior British diplomat of Indian origin has resigned, citing the Foreign Office's 'woke' culture and an overemphasis on international law at the expense of national security. Ameer Kotecha criticized the handling of issues like the Chagos Islands and Iran, arguing for a more Britain-first approach. He described the civil service as inefficient and out of touch with national priorities.
item.dc:creator: Naomi Canton

item.title: UAE slams Bloomberg over ‘inaccurate’ air defence report amid US–Israel war on Iran
item.description: The UAE has strongly refuted a Bloomberg report questioning its air defence capabilities, calling the claims false and misleading. Asserting its possession of diverse, multi-layered systems and robust munitions, the ministry stressed its unwavering operational readiness. This strong rebuttal highlights the nation's commitment to controlling its security narrative amidst regional tensions and calls for responsible journalism.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: “Erika scam a genius like Charlie”: Candace Owens’ explanation about Charlie Kirk’s relationship choices sparks controversy
item.description: Candace Owens’ comments about Charlie Kirk’s relationship with Erika Kirk have sparked online backlash after journalist Natalie Jean Beisner criticized her remarks. Owens argued that intelligence does not prevent people from making mistakes in relationships. Critics say the discussion is insensitive given Kirk’s death, while supporters believe Owens was explaining how emotions can cloud judgment.
item.dc:creator: Barsha Dutta

item.title: High alert in the Gulf: Kuwait arrests two for viral videos mocking armed forces, air defence efforts on social media amid Iran-US-Israel war
item.description: Kuwait has arrested two individuals for mocking its armed forces and air defence on social media amidst escalating US–Israel war with Iran. This move signals a stricter enforcement of public order and national security laws. Authorities emphasise the need for unity and respect for security forces as the nation actively defends its airspace against airborne threats.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Saudia extends flight suspensions until March 6: 8 destinations affected amid Iran-US–Israel conflict
item.description: Saudia has extended flight suspensions to eight key destinations until March 6, 2026. This decision stems from ongoing regional tensions and airspace closures due to US–Israel–Iran conflict, impacting commercial air travel. The airline is contacting affected passengers directly. Travellers are advised to verify flight status before heading to the airport. Other regional carriers also face similar disruptions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Middle East crisis: Trump rates US war effort ‘15 out of 10’; vows to push on against Iran
item.description: US President Trump declared the campaign against Iran "about a 15" on a scale of 10, citing success in decimating Iranian leadership and missile capabilities. He reiterated the goal of preventing nuclear weapons, vowing to continue joint operations with Israel despite escalating regional conflict, rising oil prices, and domestic criticism.

item.title: Arkansas father accused of killing daughter’s alleged rapist wins GOP nomination for sheriff
item.description: An Arkansas father, awaiting trial for allegedly killing his daughter's accused sexual predator, has won the Republican nomination for county sheriff. Aaron Spencer defeated the incumbent, securing over 53% of the vote.

item.title: UAE flights resume but not fully: 5 airlines begin limited services amid Iran–US–Israel conflict
item.description: UAE airlines are operating limited flights amid regional airspace closures due to escalating Iran-US-Israel tensions. Authorities are using emergency corridors to resume services cautiously, prioritizing stranded passengers. Most regular flights remain suspended, with airlines extending cancellations as safety assessments continue. Travelers are urged to verify flight status before heading to airports.

item.title: Stocks empty or strategic move? Iran firing fewer missiles, says top US General
item.description: Iran's missile and drone attacks have significantly decreased, according to US military chief General Dan Caine. Despite this, Washington is expanding its offensive deeper into Iranian territory. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth declared the US is winning, highlighting a submarine sinking an Iranian warship. The conflict has widened regionally, causing displacement and economic shockwaves.

item.title: 'Is it still America or Israel first': Iran's Ali Larijani accuses Trump of dragging US in 'unfair war'
item.description: Iran's top security official, Ali Larijani, accused President Trump of initiating an "unfair war" and vowed retaliation for the reported killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Larijani stated Iran will not negotiate with Washington amid escalating regional conflict, questioning Trump's "America First" policy after significant US troop casualties.

item.title: Dubai under tension? Indian TV star Erica Fernandes shares on-ground reality from UAE emirate amid Iran-US-Israel clashes, sparks debate
item.description: Indian TV actor Erica J Fernandes shared a Dubai video featuring intercepted aerial threats alongside confident UAE rulers, captioned 'Habibi you're still welcome to Dubai.' Her clarification emphasised her personal experience of safety and efficient handling of regional tensions amid Iran and US-Israel clashes, sparking debate on social media's role in portraying geopolitical realities.

item.title: Who is Mothin Ali? Why is the Green Party leader fighting with Keir Starmer?
item.description: Leeds councillor Mothin Ali, Green Party co-deputy leader, faces controversy over statements on Israel and international conflicts. His 2023 tweet about "white supremacist European settler colonialism" and a 2025 remark calling an IDF-serving rabbi an "animal" drew sharp criticism. A 2026 parliamentary clash with PM Keir Starmer further intensified scrutiny.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Watch: Louisiana worker dangling from fiery cherry picker before plunging to ground
item.description: A harrowing incident unfolded in Baton Rouge as a utility worker dangled precariously from his harness after his bucket truck erupted in flames. Thick smoke billowed as the man struggled for security high above the street. Coworkers raced to help before he ultimately fell and was hospitalized with severe injuries. Officials suspect mechanical failure.
